After the incident, Poland asked Ukraine to provide better information about the movements of its aircraft, and the data exchange system between the two sides was improved.

IRAN ASKS RUSSIA FOR ITS ADVANCED GERAN DRONES, TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER COMES FULL CIRCLE
Iran has asked Moscow to supply its newest Russian-developed Geran attack drones for use against Israel and the United States, according to the Financial Times, citing Western security officials and a person close to the Kremlin. It remains unclear whether Russia has agreed to the latest request.
Iran originally supplied Russia with the Shahed technology. Russia then spent four years combat-testing, modifying and mass-producing the platform in Ukraine and Tehran now reportedly wants Russia’s evolved versions back.
The latest jet-powered Geran variants are faster, carry larger warheads and incorporate improved targeting, communications and resistance to electronic warfare. Russia’s adaptation of the Iranian design has become so extensive that CSIS recently concluded that Russia has effectively mastered the platform through continuous battlefield-driven development

Newly declassified footage shows the rescue of two U.S. Air Force officers after their F-15E multirole fighter was shot down over Iran in April.
The two pilots ejected and landed roughly five miles apart in mountainous terrain south of Isfahan as Iranian forces searched for them.
Alpha was recovered eight hours after ejecting in a risky daytime recovery mission involving 21 U.S. aircraft.
Bravo remained behind Iranian lines for roughly two days. He suffered a broken back and other injuries after his damaged parachute caused a hard landing, but still managed to climb a 7,000-foot mountain ridge before two Air Force pararescuemen reached him and brought him to a U.S. Air Force HH-60W Jolly Green II helicopter.

Denmark and Italy push forward on migration control.
The EU Parliament has voted to back new rules for return hubs outside Europe. This allows faster returns of rejected asylum seekers and irregular migrants to third countries, speeding up deportations and strengthening border management.
Led by efforts from Denmark’s Mette Frederiksen and Italy’s Giorgia Meloni, Europe is moving toward more pragmatic, effective migration policies.
